title: Probe steward weekly capture
content:
Weekly capture: probe steward (2026-09-21)

Attendees: Erin, Samir, Jules, Talia, Liam (30m)
Context: quick sync to triage quant onboarding experiments, surface eval regressions, and coordinate a short mitigation plan for a KV-cache incompatibility seen on 4-bit builds.

1) Highlights / quick wins
- Microbatch throughput on 4-bit int4_hybrid build improved by ~1.6x for real-time chat traces (seq len 128, batch 8) when we switched to the new tiled-kernel path (PR 128). Memory headroom up ~2.4x which allows keeping two active model variants per device for A/B. (Samir ran the perf harness)
- Small eval set (SQuAD-like QA slices + 100 conversational prompts) shows only a mild nEM drop (mean -1.3%) for int4_hybrid vs fp16 on the compact-sparrow-3B candidate after re-tuning layernorm scaling. Promising for dedicated capacity use-case.

2) Failures / pain points observed
- KV-cache misalignment on long-context (>2048) sequences with int4_hybrid kernels. Symptoms: token repetition and context truncation when requests hit a warm-started cache lane after a scale-up event. Repro steps attached below. (Filed ML-3421)
- Deterministic regression in our reranking eval (MRR) for some prompts where numeric precision in the last-token logits flips answer order; appears correlated with layernorm shard ordering differences between fp16 and quantized forward path.
- End-to-end latency tail (95th) increased by ~12% in cloud-hosted microbenchmark when enabling tiled kernels without adjusting the batching window. Likely caused by non-optimal batching strategy for short chat bursts.

3) Repro steps (KV-cache bug)
- Environment: int4_hybrid build from rw-quant branch PR/128, runtime v3.7.2-rc
- Model: compact-sparrow-3B, sequence setup: prime with 1536 tokens, then send 8 single-token continuations across two concurrent connections.
- Trigger: scale up (add instance) during the continuations -> observe repeated tokens / sudden context loss after the first scale event.
- Quick note: same trace on fp16/float32 path does NOT show the issue.

4) Triage notes (what we tried / findings)
- Samir: Instrumented KV buffer offsets; found off-by-8-word alignment introduced when recomputing cache offsets during the tiled-kernel fallback path. Patch candidate reduces misalignments but still leaves occasional mismatch for certain layer splits.
- Jules: Re-ran rerank eval with deterministic seeding and layernorm-shift correction (multiply by 0.998 instead of 1.0) — MRR regression reduced but not eliminated. Suspect accumulation order differences in fused kernels.
- Talia: Experimented with keeping microbatch window fixed for chat bursts; tail latency returns to baseline but throughput drops for larger batches. Trade-off decision needed for hosted tier.

5) Short-term mitigation plan (next 72h)
- Hotfix KV-cache alignment guard: add double-check after cache-merge and fallback to safe fp16 path if offsets misalign (owner: Samir, due: 2026-09-23). Jira ML-3421 -> blocker flag if reproduces in prod traces.
- Eval sweep: run expanded rerank + safety prompts across int4_hybrid and int8 fallback variants (owner: Jules, due: 2026-09-24). Capture exact prompts that flip order and attach to ML-3490.
- Batching config: revert tiled-kernel batching-window increase and ship a config toggle (owner: Talia, due: 2026-09-22) for hosted-api to minimize latency tail for PLG tier.

6) Medium-term work (next sprint)
- Kernel correctness audit: deeper pass on fused layernorm and attention numeric ordering (owner: eng-quant-team, primary: Samir + Jules). Blocker tasks: identify layers with non-associative ops that differ between quantized and fp16 flows.
- Model onboarding checklist update: add step to run long-context stress tests (>=8k tokens) and scale-up scale-down tests under incremental load. Update confluence checklist (owner: Erin, due: 2026-09-30).
- Automated prompt-preservation eval: create a small harness that tracks reference completions for 10k critical prompts and flags semantic deltas > threshold. (owner: Talia, due: 2026-10-04).

7) Data/Eval artifacts to attach
- Perf harness traces: s3://rw-qa/quant/probe/sep21/throughput-batch8.log
- Rerank diff CSV: s3://rw-qa/quant/probe/sep21/rerank-diff.csv
- Repro script: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-quant/actions/repro_kv_bug.sh

8) Open questions / discussion points
- Is a staged rollout with int8 fallback safer than int4-hybrid primary for the PLG hosted tier? (risk vs cost tradeoffs)
- Can we add simple runtime assertions that compare a small set of fp16 reference outputs for every model startup as a smoke check? Cost vs reliability trade-off?
- How urgent: do we require a full kernel rollback for int4 until correctness audit complete, or can the hotfix guard suffice for customer traffic?

9) Notes to self (informal)
- Capture exact prompt that triggered the rerank flip — it’s in rerank-diff.csv row 87. Also check slack thread #quant-kv for a short clip Sam posted at 10:12.
- If hotfix triggers safe-fallback often, coordinate with infra on capacity plan (dedicated pools will need buffer).

Action items recap:
- Samir: KV-cache guard hotfix + unit tests (due 9/23)
- Jules: Expanded rerank & safety sweep, attach flipping prompts to ML-3490 (due 9/24)
- Talia: Batching toggle config for hosted-api, monitor tail on canary (due 9/22)
- Erin: Update onboarding checklist + long-context stress step (due 9/30)
- Liam: Run the 8k token stress harness on private deployment (due 9/25)

Next sync: Mon 2026-09-27, 10:00am PT (15m) — quick status + unblock review.
